record.provider: Air Cluster — commercial product that advertises combining several accounts (incl. accounts from the same provider)

free_tier.stated: 'Air Cluster allows you to add several accounts from the same server (e.g., three different OneDrive accounts) and combine their capacity into one single cluster.'

egress.terms: Client-side; files are read from each provider directly. Optional client-side encryption.

record.tooling: Windows desktop app (AirCluster-Installer.exe). No API, no Linux, no rclone backend.
record.chaining: N accounts, including N accounts of the same provider, presented as one large-capacity 'cluster'. This is the clearest commercial statement of the hypothesis: 'Unlike standard file managers, Air Cluster allows you to create a "Cluster", which combines the storage space of all your cloud accounts. This lets you manage the total space as if it were a single, large-capacity hard drive.'
record.limits_note: Windows graphical interface only without public programmatic API access. Documentation does not specify whether large files are striped across accounts or distributed at the whole-file level.
record.reliability_note: Closed-source commercial; cannot audit placement or repair behaviour.

evidence.proved: 'Can I use multiple accounts from the same provider? Yes... combine their capacity into one single cluster'; 'manage the total space as if it were a single, large-capacity hard drive' — the vendor's own copy, quoted verbatim; it describes several accounts combined into one pool

record.notes: 'Air Cluster allows you to add several accounts from the same server (e.g., three different OneDrive accounts) and combine their capacity into one single cluster.'

dead_end.why: 'Air Cluster allows you to add several accounts from the same server (e.g., three different OneDrive accounts) and combine their capacity into one single cluster.'
